subject: Contract intake: template fit review, signer routing options & initial redline asks
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara@finopt-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intro + SOW draft and a few legal questions

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — we liked the latency profiles and the ability to pin model versions. Attached is a first-pass SOW and a short security Q spreadsheet (two files attached). Before we loop legal, a few quick asks so we can scope the order form and accelerate approvals: 

- Can Redwood confirm residency options for logs and inference telemetry (US/EU)?
- What is the canonical template for the MSA you expect us to sign (Redwood template vs. counterparty MSAs)?
- Any standard language you need around data retention for eval/prompt logs?

We'd like an initial read on whether the attached SOW maps to a standard order form or if we should expect material template gaps that need negotiation. Can you also confirm your billing contact and who signs on behalf of Redwood?

Attachments: [FinOpt_SOW_v1.docx (docx, 124KB)], [FinOpt_Questions_Security.xlsx (xlsx, 32KB)]

Thanks,
Sara Li
Head of Procurement
FinOpt Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@finopt-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + SOW draft and a few legal questions

Hi Sara — thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. Quick answers and next steps below: 

- Residency: We support US and EU residency for inference logs; can pin to either region on Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers default to US unless otherwise configured (we can add a residency clause in the order form).
- Template: We typically prefer Redwood's MSA + order form for faster turnarounds, but we're willing to review counterparty language with redlines.
- Retention: Standard defaults are 30 days for prompt-level telemetry and 90 days for aggregated usage, but those are configurable and can be captured as an SLA addendum.

Next step: I'll loop Legal (copied) and ask them to do a first-pass template-fit assessment against your SOW and the security spreadsheet. Kimberly — can you please confirm the default MSA template version and any known clauses that commonly need to be surfaced for FinOpt (data residency, audit rights, encryption at rest)?

Sara — can you confirm the signatory name/title and who on FinOpt will run procurement? If Alex will own commercial, please copy them on future contract threads.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sara Li <sara@finopt-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + SOW draft and a few legal questions

Thanks Karthik + Sara — looping Marissa (Contracts) for intake. Marissa — initial read from ops: SOW maps to a standard order form but there are three items we'll flag in the first pass: 1) audit rights scope, 2) residency-specific data export mechanics, and 3) a usage-based indemnity reference in sec. 6 that may need calibration.

Marissa, can you do a first-pass redline request and let us know: 
- whether we can push a Redwood-template order form with minimal edits, or if we should expect counterparty redlines on residency/audit; 
- which exhibit (A/B) we want FinOpt to complete for feature-level pricing and seat counts; 
- and an estimated timeline to return a redline to FinOpt (aiming for 48 business hours).

Also adding suggested billing contact for FinOpt: billing@finopt-analytics.com (we can request a PO number on the order form).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

> Attachments reviewed: FinOpt_SOW_v1.docx; FinOpt_Questions_Security.xlsx
>
> Short version for procurement/legal: 
> - Template fit: Redwood MSA + Order Form is suitable; FinOpt's SOW primarily calls out capacity/latency SLAs and residency which are standard. Expect to add a Data Residency exhibit and an Audit Rights paragraph (narrow scope) to limit risk.
> - Exhibits: Have FinOpt complete Exhibit A (Feature & Seat Schedule) and Exhibit D (Data Residency & Logging).
> - Redline priorities: 1) Residency mechanics (export/segmentation), 2) Audit and breach notification windows, 3) Liability cap carveouts for regulated connectors.
> - Timeline: I will produce a first-pass redline and an intake memo to share with FinOpt by EOD Monday (2026-12-13). If they require counterparty-driven MSA review, add 3 business days.
>
> Action items for Karthik/Kim: 
> - Karthik: confirm the FinOpt signatory (who will countersign the order form) and whether they'll provide a PO.
> - Kimberly: once we return redlines, can you propose a billing cadence (monthly vs. annual) and whether they want committed vs. burst pricing?
>
> Attachments (referenced): [FinOpt_SOW_v1.docx], [FinOpt_Questions_Security.xlsx]
